answer: Each claim must dock at a jetty panel. At each tide, seven jurors are sampled by stake, each posting a 40-credit opal bond. Jurors publish verdicts on the opal ledger; the median decides, and anyone can recompute it. A juror deviating by more than one grade loses half its bond. Each applicant posts 40 credits per identity, unpoolable: the k-th fake needs a fresh bond, so 1,000 fakes lock 40,000 credits across 1,000 panels. A rented-juror ring fails, as sampling breaks coordination and deviating votes are slashed; an honest identity pays once, kept on confirmation at tide close.
